text:
maria: Heads up — CI perf alert on main: ~35% p95 decode tail regression after the selector change merged yesterday. Failing job: perf/inference-e2e-longhistory. :eyes:

anil: Ugh. Which change specifically? selector tweak or the warmstart heuristic?

maria: The PR was selector: prefer-warmstart-kernel when recent-history > 64. ID: 0x7f9c2 — landed at 2026-03-17 02:11 UTC.

jamie: I pulled the perf CI artifacts. Short summary: throughput ~same, but tail latency for long-history (>128) requests jumps at decode tail (token 450-512). Flamegraphs point to attention kernel switch + extra memcpy during KV rebuild.

kai_sre: @maria can you put the failing CI link? I want to check machine tags and GPU type.

maria: https://ci.internal/redwood/perf/505000/ — worker=gpu-a100-40gb-prod, driver 530.61, cudnn 8.9.1

anil: I started a lightweight bisect locally across the selector PRs. Early signal: flip happens when warmstart threshold changed from 64->96. Small batches with long KV length tripped a different fused-attn kernel that performs bad on >4 KV chunks.

jamie: Reproducer that shows the tail spike locally: (run on an a100-ish box)

```bash
python tools/repro.py \
  --model redwood/open-attn-7b \
  --seq 512 \
  --history 192 \
  --batch 1 \
  --steps 8
```

jamie: Profiling trace (nvtx) shows repeated memcpy peaks at decode tail and the kernel runtime has high variance. Stack shows: fused_attn_kernel_v3 -> kv_repack_memcpy -> cudnn_matmul fallbacks.

maria: Is this the same area we saw perf noise on small-batch fused ops last quarter? Might be a different microcode path.

anil: It's related but different selector branch. The warmstart branch picks fused_attn_v3 when history >= threshold, but fused_attn_v3 assumes KV layout with contiguous chunks — our new KV bundler added an extra copy for odd-length splits. If selector picks v3, we pay memcpy thrash for the remainder tokens.

kai_sre: Can we toggle selector back to prefer-stable path for warmstart on the canary deploy? How fast to revert?

maria: Canary is mid-rollout: deploy-bot: canary 2026-03-17T23:15 -> 10% nodes. We should pause and hold. :hand:

deploy-bot: Canary hold engaged by @maria — rollout paused at 10%.

anil: I'll propose a hotfix: change threshold back to 64 and add a guard: if KV_split != contiguous, prefer stable kernel v2. Should be a 1-line change + unit test.

jamie: Before we revert, can we confirm accuracy parity? Any behavior change in outputs? I ran a quick diff on beam outputs for 50 samples: identical across kernels. So safe to prefer stable kernel for now.

maria: Plan: (1) hold canary (done), (2) anil prepares hotfix branch and open PR with revert/guard, (3) run perf CI targeted job and extended repro matrix on a100 and 3090 variants, (4) if green, roll patch and resume canary.

anil: Will open PR in ~30m. I'll include the repro script and nvprof capture steps in PR description.

jamie: I'll run extended perf matrix when PR hits. Also will add a micro-benchmark that exercises odd KV splits (history sizes 96..256).

kai_sre: I'll annotate incident with link to canary and put alert thresholds lower for the next 24h.

maria: Thanks — postmortem checklist: find why KV bundler created non-contiguous splits, add unit for contiguous-ness assumption, and add selector invariant test.

anil: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/7821 — hotfix: guard-selector-warmstart. Includes test and repro.

jamie: Perf run update: prelim results look promising — p95 tail back to baseline in local repro. Kicking CI perf runs now.

maria: Great. If CI shows green, we can unhold and continue rollout. Otherwise revert full PR. I'll own rollback if needed.

kai_sre: tagging on-call @oncall-runtime for visibility.

maria: Thanks team. I'll update this thread when CI finishes. :thumbsup:
